verses.author: model_A
verses.text: My grandmother's hands remember a language I never learned.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the flour still knows
when it's ready —
some silence tastes like bread

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
I write the words down anyway,
hoping ink remembers
what my mouth forgot.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
steam fogs the window
where I trace her name
in a language of one finger

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the glass clears too fast —
already the shape of it
gone back to breath

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
what the breath knew
the table doesn't ask for —
just sets itself again

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
morning light finds
the same four cups waiting —
no one counts the empty one

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the fifth cup
lives in the cupboard's dark—
dust learning its shape

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
someone's hand
almost reaches the shelf—
then remembers the season

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
still, the kettle sings
its old two-note song—
for four, or for one more

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
steam fogs the window—
a name almost said
settles back into breath

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the porch light stays on—
no one asks anymore
who it's waiting for

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
snow gathers on the mat
where boots used to wait—
now just the shape of patience

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
she sweeps it anyway
each morning, the same corner—
clean space needs no reason

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the broom leans by the door
learning its own kind of stillness—
spring will ask nothing of it

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
a bird lands on the handle
tests it like a question—
no one home to answer
